identification.summary: Curly COMrades is a cluster Bitdefender first described in August 2025 as a previously unknown, Russia-aligned espionage group targeting Georgia and Moldova [S1][S3]. Bitdefender says the name comes from heavy use of the curl utility for command and control and data transfer and from hijacking of COM objects [S3]. A November 2025 Bitdefender report described the group hiding malware in a Hyper-V virtual machine on Windows hosts [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Bitdefender has tracked the activity since mid-2024; the earliest confirmed MucorAgent use is November 2023 [S3]. Reporting on the Hyper-V activity describes the cluster as active since late 2023 [S5].
identification.notes: Name is Bitdefender's. No Microsoft name or MITRE group ID is established in the sources gathered. Amazon reports infrastructure overlap with APT44/Sandworm-linked activity but frames the clusters as possibly complementary, not identical [S7][S8]. One aggregator lists Curly COMrades as an alias of APT44; that conflicts with Amazon's framing and was not adopted.

attribution.sponsor: Bitdefender describes the group as Russia-aligned, operating in support of Russian interests [S1][S3]. Amazon assesses that the broader activity it tracked is associated with Russia's GRU and says Curly COMrades infrastructure overlaps with it [S7][S8]. No government has attributed Curly COMrades by name in the sources gathered.
attribution.confidence: Bitdefender stresses there are no strong overlaps with known Russian APT groups [S3]. Security Affairs labels the Russia link as alleged [S5]. Amazon states high confidence for GRU association of its own activity cluster (via Sandworm/APT44 infrastructure overlap), and hedges that the two clusters may be complementary operations within a broader GRU campaign [S7][S8]. That is Amazon's assessment and is not a confirmed merger of clusters.
attribution.basis: Bitdefender technical analysis and victimology (Georgia, Moldova) [S1][S3]; Amazon infrastructure overlap, including IP 91.99.25[.]54 per secondary coverage [S7][S8].

objectives: Bitdefender states the group's main aim is persistent access to networks and stolen credentials, in support of Russian interests [S1][S3].

targeting.notes: Bitdefender observed focused attacks against judicial and government bodies in Georgia and an energy distribution company in Moldova [S1][S3]. Victims in the Hyper-V report were not named; Georgia's CERT-GE assisted the investigation [S2]. Amazon's wider cluster targeted energy, telecom and technology providers [S7]; that is a separate cluster and is not merged here.

capabilities.summary: Bitdefender reports repeated attempts to extract the NTDS database from domain controllers and to dump LSASS memory, with Mimikatz and DCSync cited in coverage [S1][S3]. Proxy and tunnel tools (Resocks, SSH, Stunnel) provide multiple entry points, and remote commands were often run with Atexec [S1][S3]. MucorAgent is a custom three-stage .NET backdoor that runs AES-encrypted PowerShell, bypasses AMSI, and persists by hijacking CLSIDs tied to the NGEN component via an apparently inactive scheduled task [S3]. The initial access vector was not determined [S3]. In the later campaign the group enabled Hyper-V on selected Windows 10 hosts to run a minimal Alpine Linux VM (about 120MB disk, 256MB memory) named to resemble WSL, hosting CurlyShell (libcurl reverse shell) and CurlCat (reverse proxy tunneling SSH as HTTP), which let activity largely evade host-based EDR [S2][S5]. Attackers used a compromised website as a proxy for their real infrastructure [S5].

campaigns.summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence reports a GRU-associated campaign against energy and other sectors and notes infrastructure overlap with Curly COMrades, possibly complementary operations.

diamond.adversary: Russia-aligned cluster per Bitdefender; possible complementary relationship with a GRU-associated cluster per Amazon [S3][S7].
diamond.capability: MucorAgent, CurlyShell, CurlCat, Resocks/SSH/Stunnel tunnels, Atexec, NTDS and LSASS credential theft, NGEN COM hijacking, Hyper-V VM abuse [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: A compromised website used as proxy for actor infrastructure; curl-based C2; IP 91.99.25[.]54 overlaps with Amazon's cluster [S5][S8].
diamond.victim: Georgian judicial and government bodies; Moldovan energy distribution company [S1][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Targets sit in countries facing major geopolitical shifts, consistent with collection supporting Russian interests per Bitdefender [S1].
diamond.technology: Windows domain controllers and Windows 10 hosts with Hyper-V available; EDR products that do not see inside guest VMs [S2].

gaps: Initial access vector is not determined in Bitdefender's August 2025 report [S3].
Relationship to Sandworm/APT44: Amazon suggests complementary operations; Bitdefender sees no strong overlap with known Russian groups. Unresolved [S3][S7].
No Microsoft actor name, MITRE group ID, or government attribution found.
Victims of the November 2025 campaign are unnamed [S2].
No campaign activity after December 2025 found in searches.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is Windows domain controllers (NTDS), hosts that can enable Hyper-V, and government or energy networks in Georgia and Moldova; coalition partner networks in the region share this exposure [S1][S3]. STEP 2: Host-level virtualization hides implants from EDR, and the initial access vector is unknown, narrowing defender visibility [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Template is initial access (unknown), proxy/tunnel tools, credential theft from domain controllers, COM-hijack persistence, then a hidden VM with reverse shell and proxy [S1][S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued credential-focused espionage against regional government, judicial and energy targets. MDCOA is use of the same persistence on partner or US-supported energy and government networks, or coordinated use with GRU-associated access operations as Amazon speculates [S7]. Candidate indicators: Hyper-V role newly enabled on workstations, unexpected VMs named like WSL, NGEN-related CLSID changes and disabled-looking scheduled tasks, NTDS/LSASS access, outbound curl-style traffic to compromised sites [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: add hypervisor and VM-inventory telemetry on Windows endpoints to hunt plans, since EDR may not see guest activity [S2]. (2) Authorities: partner-network hunting in Georgia or Moldova depends on host-nation consent; Bitdefender's work relied on CERT-GE cooperation [S2]. (3) Mission assurance: protect domain controller credentials for energy and government mission systems against NTDS/LSASS theft [S1]. (4) Coordination: attribution is contested between Bitdefender and Amazon, so share indicators with partners and vendors rather than waiting on naming [S3][S7].

provenance.importedSummary: Curly COMrades is a threat actor identified by Amazon Threat Intelligence and Bitdefender, believed to operate in support of Russian interests. They employ techniques such as Hyper-V abuse for EDR evasion and utilize proxy tools like Resocks, SSH, and Stunnel to gain access to internal networks. Their activities include repeated attempts to extract the NTDS database from domain controllers and establishing covert access through virtualization features on compromised Windows 10 machines.
